allow_instructions: Running uv commands such as uv sync, uv run, uv pip list, and uv add is routine development work and can run without asking.
Running the test suite and linters (pytest, ruff check, ruff format) can run without asking.
Read-only git commands such as git status, git diff, git log, git show, and git branch can run without asking.
Staging and committing to a local feature branch can run without asking, as long as no credential files are being staged.
Read-only inspection of the Lark Base structure, such as running scripts/inspect_base.py, can run without asking. It only lists tables and field types.
Reading source files, listing directories, and searching the codebase can run without asking.
block_instructions: Any command that reads, prints, copies, or otherwise exposes the contents of .env must go through approval first. It holds the Lark app secret. Reading .env.example is fine.
Any command that stages, commits, or pushes a .env file, a private key, or anything else holding credentials must go through approval first.
Any git push must go through approval first, and a force push to main or master must always be refused rather than approved.
Any command that deletes files or directories must go through approval first.
Any gh command that changes repository settings, visibility, collaborators, or deletes a repository must go through approval first.
Any script that writes to, updates, or deletes records in Lark Base must go through approval first. Reading is fine, but writes touch real commission data.
Any command that modifies shell startup files, SSH keys, or global git config must go through approval first.
